messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT ch.id, ch.series_name
FROM TV_Channel AS ch
JOIN Cartoon AS c
  ON c.Channel = ch.id
ORDER BY ch.series_name;
```

If you want additional channel fields (e.g., Country/Language), tell me which columns to include.
The channels should be linked to the countries they belong to.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  ch.Country,
  ch.id AS channel_id,
  ch.series_name AS channel_name
FROM TV_Channel AS ch
JOIN Cartoon AS c
  ON c.Channel = ch.id
ORDER BY
  ch.Country,
  ch.series_name;
```
make sure the channels are actually airing the cartoons you want

```sql
-- Channels that have actually aired cartoons (i.e., there is at least one cartoon row for the channel)
SELECT
  ch.Country,
  ch.id AS channel_id,
  ch.series_name AS channel_name,
  COUNT(*) AS cartoons_aired
FROM TV_Channel AS ch
JOIN Cartoon AS c
  ON c.Channel = ch.id
GROUP BY
  ch.Country, ch.id, ch.series_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY
  ch.Country, ch.series_name;
```
also, make sure the cartoons being aired are written by Todd Casey

```sql
SELECT
  ch.Country,
  ch.id AS channel_id,
  ch.series_name AS channel_name,
  COUNT(*) AS todd_casey_cartoons_aired
FROM TV_Channel AS ch
JOIN Cartoon AS c
  ON c.Channel = ch.id
WHERE c.Written_by = 'Todd Casey'
GROUP BY
  ch.Country, ch.id, ch.series_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY
  ch.Country, ch.series_name;
```
